courses.description:
**Recorded lessons with live classes every week.** Short videos, a quiz after each topic, a written task with feedback, and study sheets to download.

Many people study English for years and still cannot build a correct sentence with confidence. This course starts again from the beginning, the right way: you learn how English is put together, one piece at a time, and you use each piece before moving on.

## Who is this course for?

- You studied English at school but still feel unsure of the basics.
- You memorised grammar rules that did not help you speak or write.
- You want a strong base before an exam course such as IELTS.
- You tried other courses and want a clear, step-by-step path.

## Frequently asked questions

### How do I pay?

Send the fee with bKash or Nagad, then enter the transaction ID on the enrollment page. We confirm payments within a day and your course opens in your student portal.

### Do I need a laptop?

No. Every lesson works on a phone or tablet. A laptop is optional.

### Can I ask questions?

Yes. Ask under any lesson and the teacher replies there, where your classmates can read the answer too.

### Do I get a certificate?

Yes. Finish every lesson and your certificate is ready to download, with a number anyone can check.

posts.title: Five minutes a day beats two hours on Friday
posts.excerpt: Why short daily practice works better than one long session, and how to start.
posts.body:
Most learners plan one long study session a week. Most of them skip it.

A language is a habit, and habits are built by repetition, not by effort. Five minutes every day gives your memory seven chances a week to keep a new word. Two hours on Friday gives it one.

## What five minutes looks like

- Read one short paragraph aloud.
- Write three sentences about your day.
- Review yesterday's five new words before learning five more.

## Make it hard to skip

Tie it to something you already do: after breakfast, on the bus, before you check your phone at night. The best time is the one you will actually keep.

Start today. Not with two hours. With five minutes.

posts.title: How to stop translating in your head
posts.excerpt: Three habits that help you think in English instead of translating every sentence.
posts.body:
If you build every sentence in your own language first and then translate it, you will always be slow, and your sentences will carry the shape of the other language.

## 1. Learn phrases, not single words

Do not learn *interested*. Learn *I am interested in*. A phrase arrives ready to use, with its grammar already inside it.

## 2. Name what you see

Walking down the street, name things in English, silently: *a red bus, a closed shop, two students waiting*. No translation is needed for what is in front of you.

## 3. Allow simple sentences

You translate because you want to say something complicated. Say something simpler instead. *I was late. The bus did not come.* Two short, correct sentences beat one long broken one.

It feels slow for a few weeks. Then one day you notice a whole thought arrived in English.

posts.title: Say it wrong first
posts.excerpt: Mistakes are how speaking improves. Here is how to make more of them, on purpose.
posts.body:
Nobody learns to swim by reading about water. And nobody learns to speak by waiting until their sentences are perfect.

## Why mistakes help

When you say something wrong and are corrected, you remember the correction far better than a rule you read. The small sting is what makes it stay.

## Three safe places to be wrong

- **Alone:** describe your day aloud for one minute. Record it. Listen once.
- **With a classmate:** agree to speak only English for ten minutes, and to correct each other kindly.
- **In class:** ask your question in English, even if it comes out crooked. That is what the class is for.

## Keep a mistake list

Write down each correction you receive. Read the list once a week. You will see the same five mistakes again and again, and then, one by one, you will stop making them.

pages.title: About us
pages.body:
Alif Academy teaches English to learners who want to use it: in an exam hall, in an office, in a message to a client.

## Our mission

Good English teaching should not depend on where you live. We teach online so that a student in a small town gets the same lessons, the same teacher and the same feedback as one in the capital.

## How we teach

- **One idea at a time.** Each lesson covers a single point, and you use it before moving on.
- **Reasons, not rules.** We explain why an answer is right, so the next question is easier.
- **Feedback from a person.** Your written work is read and answered by your teacher.

## Our story

The academy began as evening classes for a handful of job seekers. The classes filled, then filled again, and moving online was the only way to say yes to everyone who asked.

## Our name

*Alif* is the first letter of the alphabet: where every reader begins.

pages.title: Privacy policy
pages.body:
Last updated: November 2026

Your privacy matters to us. This policy explains what we collect, how we use it and how we protect it when you use this website and your student account.

## Information we collect

- **Account details:** your name, email address and, if you give it, your phone number.
- **Payment details:** the bKash or Nagad number you paid from and the transaction ID you enter. We don't store card details or PINs; payments are made in the bKash or Nagad app.
- **Your learning:** the lessons you finish, your quiz results, your questions, and the assignments you hand in.
- **Sign-in:** your password is stored only in a scrambled (hashed) form that we cannot read.

## How we use your information

- To confirm your payment and open your course
- To give you your lessons, feedback and certificate
- To answer your questions and send password-reset emails

## Sharing your information

We do not sell your information. It is seen only by your teacher and our support staff, or shared when the law requires it. A certificate can be checked by anyone who has its number; it shows your name, the course and the date.

## Your choices

You can ask to see, correct or delete your personal data. Message us and we will do it, where the law allows.

## Changes to this policy

This policy may be updated. The current version is always shown here with its date.
